questions.title: Technical specification
questions.text: Define the term **technical specification** of a new system.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- A document listing the hardware and software needed to run the system (1)
- with a reason / justification for each item (1)

points.criterion: A document listing the hardware and software needed to run the system
with a reason / justification for each item

scheme.model_answer: A document that lists the hardware and software the new system needs and explains why each was chosen.

questions.title: Minimum RAM
questions.text: A new system needs an operating system (minimum 4 GB RAM), a DBMS (2 GB) and the library application (1 GB), all running at the same time. Which is the **smallest suitable** amount of RAM for the specification?

questions.title: Devices from inputs and outputs
questions.text: A supermarket is introducing a new checkout system. Customers' products are scanned and each customer gets a paper receipt. State **two** devices that must be in the technical specification and why each is needed.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Barcode scanner — to read products quickly / accurately (1)
- Receipt (thermal) printer — to print receipts (1)

points.criterion: Barcode scanner — to read products quickly / accurately
Receipt (thermal) printer — to print receipts

scheme.model_answer: A barcode scanner to read the product codes, and a thermal receipt printer to print each receipt.

questions.title: Choosing storage
questions.text: Explain why an **SSD** might be chosen instead of an HDD for the computer that runs a school's database.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- SSD is faster to read / write data (1)
- so searches / queries / loading are quicker for many users (or: more reliable, no moving parts) (1)

points.criterion: SSD is faster to read / write data
so searches / queries / loading are quicker for many users (or: more reliable, no moving parts)

scheme.model_answer: An SSD reads and writes data much faster than an HDD, so the database answers queries more quickly.

questions.title: Allowing a margin
questions.text: Explain why a designer specifies hardware **above** the minimum requirements of the software.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- To allow for growth of data / users in future (1)
- and running several programs at once without slowing down (1)

points.criterion: To allow for growth of data / users in future
and running several programs at once without slowing down

scheme.model_answer: The amount of data and users will grow and several programs run at once, so extra capacity stops the system becoming slow.

questions.title: Software criteria
questions.text: A designer asks: *"Will this software run on the chosen hardware and operating system, and can it import our existing data?"* Which criterion is this?

questions.title: Price only
questions.text: When choosing software for a new system, it is enough to choose the cheapest product that is available.

scheme.explanation: Software must also meet the requirements and be compatible, easy to use, supported, secure and able to grow.

questions.title: Justify a DBMS
questions.text: A school chooses **MySQL** as the DBMS for its new library system. Justify this choice using **three** criteria.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Cost: free / open-source licence (1)
- Compatibility: runs on the school's OS / works with PHP and web apps (1)
- Support / scalability / security: large community, documentation, copes with more data (1)

points.criterion: Cost: free / open-source licence
Compatibility: runs on the school's OS / works with PHP and web apps
Support / scalability / security: large community, documentation, copes with more data

scheme.model_answer: MySQL is free and open-source, so there is no licence cost; it runs on the school's server and works with the PHP web interface; it has good documentation and can cope with more books and users later.

questions.title: Open-source or proprietary
questions.text: State **one** advantage and **one** disadvantage of choosing **open-source** software for a new system.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Advantage, e.g. free / can be changed to fit the system (1)
- Disadvantage, e.g. less official support / may need expert staff (1)

points.criterion: Advantage, e.g. free / can be changed to fit the system
Disadvantage, e.g. less official support / may need expert staff

scheme.model_answer: It is free and can be modified, but there may be no official technical support.

questions.title: Determining requirements
questions.text: Describe how a designer determines the **minimum hardware requirements** of a new system.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- List the software needed and read each one's minimum requirements (1)
- Take the highest value for each component / add the needs of the data (1)
- Add the peripherals needed by inputs and outputs (and a margin) (1)

points.criterion: List the software needed and read each one's minimum requirements
Take the highest value for each component / add the needs of the data
Add the peripherals needed by inputs and outputs (and a margin)

scheme.model_answer: The designer lists the software and its minimum requirements, takes the highest value for each component plus the space for the data, then adds the devices needed for the inputs and outputs and a margin for growth.

questions.title: A canteen ordering system
questions.text: A school canteen is introducing a new ordering system. Pupils order their lunch on two **touchscreen kiosks**. The orders are stored in a **database** on a server in the school office, and the kitchen **prints** each order.

parts.title: Devices
parts.text: Identify **two** input or output devices that the technical specification must include, and state why each is needed.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Touchscreen — for pupils to choose / enter orders (1)
- Printer — to print orders in the kitchen (1)

points.criterion: Touchscreen — for pupils to choose / enter orders
Printer — to print orders in the kitchen

scheme.model_answer: A touchscreen so pupils can choose their meals, and a printer in the kitchen to print each order.

parts.title: Minimum RAM
parts.text: Explain how the designer decides the minimum amount of **RAM** for the server.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Find the RAM needed by the OS, DBMS and application (1)
- add them as they run together / allow a margin for growth (1)

points.criterion: Find the RAM needed by the OS, DBMS and application
add them as they run together / allow a margin for growth

scheme.model_answer: Add the RAM needed by the operating system, the DBMS and the ordering application, which run at the same time, and allow some extra for growth.

parts.title: Justify the DBMS
parts.text: Justify the choice of DBMS software for this system using **three** criteria.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Cost / licence (1)
- Compatibility with the hardware / OS / kiosk software (1)
- Ease of use / support / security / scalability (1)

points.criterion: Cost / licence
Compatibility with the hardware / OS / kiosk software
Ease of use / support / security / scalability

scheme.model_answer: A free open-source DBMS keeps costs low, it runs on the office server and works with the kiosk software, and it has good support and can cope with more orders.

parts.title: Network
parts.text: State **one** reason why network hardware must be included in the specification.

scheme.mark_scheme: - The kiosks / kitchen printer must send orders to the database on the server (1)

points.criterion: The kiosks / kitchen printer must send orders to the database on the server

scheme.model_answer: The kiosks must send the orders to the database on the office server.

summary: Writing a technical specification — determining the minimum hardware requirements of a new system and justifying the choice of software.

blocks.content: A document that lists the **hardware and software needed** to run a new system and explains why each item was chosen.

blocks.title: Hardware to consider
rows: Heavier processing (video, databases, many users) needs a faster CPU
Number and size of programs open at once; OS minimum + application needs
Size of software + data now + expected growth + backups; SSD for speed
Keyboard, mouse, barcode scanner, camera, touchscreen
From the system's inputs (e.g. scanning products)

blocks.title: Determining the minimum requirements
items: List the **software** the system needs (OS, DBMS, applications) and read each one's **minimum requirements**.
Take the **highest** value for each component and add the needs of the **data** (size, growth).
Add the **peripherals** required by the system's inputs and outputs.
Allow a **margin** for future growth and for running several programs at once.

blocks.title: Library system for 600 students
blocks.content:
- CPU: 4-core, 2.5 GHz — runs the DBMS and the library app together.
- RAM: 8 GB — OS (4 GB) + DBMS + application.
- Storage: 256 GB SSD — software, database, daily backups.
- Barcode scanner — to scan book and student cards quickly and accurately.
- Receipt printer — to print loan slips.
- Network card — the database is shared with other computers in the school.

blocks.title: Criteria for choosing software
rows: Does it do everything in the requirements specification?
Does it run on the chosen hardware and OS? Can it import existing data?
Licence price, subscription, cost of upgrades, training
Is it easy to learn for these users? Is the interface in the right language?
Manuals, tutorials, technical support, regular updates
Can it cope with more users and data later?
Proprietary vs open source; bespoke vs off-the-shelf

blocks.title: Justification
blocks.content: "**MySQL** was chosen as the DBMS because it is **free and open-source**, runs on the school's **Linux server**, supports **many simultaneous users** and is widely used, so **documentation and support** are easy to find."
A justification needs a **reason linked to the scenario**: not just "it is good", but "it is chosen *because* the clinic needs X, and this software provides X".

lessons.title: Minimum hardware requirements; justifying the software
